The quarter-hyperbola above is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a quarter-hyperbola, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14053984/assets/d8f735790daf267a094ecd8c336d90de65d84e3985485213eb541364bd14aacd.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ],$ we get only the quarter-hyperbola.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe the required quarter-hyperbola are

$$
x=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,t\in (\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ].
$$
